sections.name: rules-first story detector (stories)
sections.title: Story detector checks
sections.what: Checks thresholds are set for cricket, football and F1. Checks stories are ordered by priority, each has receipts that match real events in the match, the source matches, and no title shows undefined or NaN. Checks the 2017 cricket tie opens with a tense finish and has a swing story, the 2008 opener has collapse and big-over stories, and has no swing story because the chase never got close. Checks football has five goals, two of them late, and missed big chances match the threshold. Checks F1 pit stops match pit-out laps and pace stories exceed the quick-lap threshold. Checks a sport with no source produces no stories.
sections.why: Likely reason: the stories must be ranked, sourced and match the moments a viewer would expect to see.
sections.watch_out: Exact title checks fail on any wording change, so titles must be updated together with these tests.

summary: Tests the story detector, which finds notable moments in real recorded matches, ranks them, and links each one to the source events that prove it.
purpose: Makes sure stories are ranked, each has real receipts, the expected key moments are found in the sample matches, and sports without a source produce nothing.
why: Likely reason: story claims must trace back to real data, so each one needs a receipt that exists in the match record.
how: Loads real recorded cricket, football and F1 fixtures and the fitted cricket win-probability model. Checks thresholds are set for each sport, stories are sorted by priority and point to real events, and the specific cricket, football and F1 stories appear with the expected counts and titles.
inputs: Recorded fixture files for cricket, football and F1, a gzipped football event file, and the fitted model file.
outputs: Lists of stories with kind, title, priority, magnitude and receipts.
risks: Exact title text is checked, so any wording change fails. A missing fixture file stops the whole suite from loading.
debug: Check that each fixture file exists. If a story count changes, compare the thresholds in the stories config with the expected values.
